answer.summary: A growth-focused leader can overgeneralize their specialty—treating every problem as growth work that should be experimented on and measured—rather than recognizing that a broader portfolio includes other kinds of product work.

sections.heading: The mistake
sections.content: Mosavat warns that when a growth leader takes over a broader portfolio, they may assume “everything is a growth problem,” and that everything should be an experiment and be measured. He says that approach is not necessarily right for other kinds of product work; leaders need to understand what matters for each category rather than applying their favorite specialty indiscriminately.

sections.heading: Why a broader portfolio calls for different thinking
sections.content: Mosavat describes four kinds of product work: feature work, growth work, product-market-fit expansion, and scaling work. Their aims differ—for example, scaling work includes trust and safety problems that arise as a product grows. He recommends curiosity, asking questions, and building a foundational understanding of each area’s goals and appropriate ways to evaluate it.
